completed: Notes sync resilience: initSync now detects local-only notes (created while offline or not yet pushed) and auto-pushes them on reconnect. Sync indicator now shows live note count for at-a-glance reassurance.
learned: Offline-first sync has two failure modes worth distinguishing: silent failed pushes (red-dot visible, user can retry) and orphan writes (note exists locally but never made it to the remote). The orphan case is the dangerous one — it looks synced because there's nothing to retry. Detecting it requires comparing local IDs against remote IDs on every init, not just tracking push failures.
session_note: Verified notes persistence by pulling the live /api/gist endpoint — found all notes intact plus 3 commits of gist version history (GitHub retains every prior state of the gist indefinitely, so even corruption is undoable). Confirmed Gist backend is fine to keep long-term with a no-expiration token; KV migration deferred as unnecessary.
aha: Orphan writes are the dangerous failure mode — failed pushes are loud, orphans are silent
struggle: Sketching the failure modes carefully enough to see the orphan case wasn't symmetric to the failed-push case
curiosity_trail: Should other localStorage-first features (theme, filter state) get the same orphan check?

completed: Defensive NaN guard in staleInfo — tracker cards now show 'Bad date format' instead of 'NaN weeks ago · stale' when a tracker's updated field can't be parsed. Diagnosed and provided fix prompts for wild-stewart-homeschool (wrong date format) and garden-app (flat priorities array instead of columns schema). Both repos confirmed fixed by Chad.
learned: JavaScript's new Date() silently returns Invalid Date on unrecognized formats — arithmetic on it produces NaN, not an error, so it can propagate deep into render logic before surfacing. Always isNaN-guard any computed value derived from a user-supplied date string. The second lesson: cross-repo tracker format drift is a real maintenance hazard when the schema lives in each repo independently — worth documenting the exact expected structure clearly so onboarding a new repo is one prompt, not trial and error.
session_note: Both bugs surfaced from Chad looking at the live dashboard. The NaN label was a defensive fix here; the actual tracker corrections happened in the respective repos via Claude Code sessions. Pattern: dashboard catches the symptom, targeted prompts fix the source.
frustration_peak: Two cards on the live dashboard both reading 'NaN weeks ago · stale' at the same time
curiosity_trail: Should the tracker schema be a published JSON schema, validated on read?

learned: Quadratic Bezier curves can be rasterized to PNG with pure stdlib Python by sampling the curve into polygon points and using ray-casting point-in-polygon — no PIL needed even for organic shapes. Three trees identified separately (vs blending into one shrub) needs both shape gaps AND tonal variation; one without the other isn't enough. The chip-syncs-composer pattern is a 'one element, two affordances' UI win — same control answers both 'show me X' and 'I want to add to X'. Naming carries weight: 'Garden' had the right metaphor but conflicted with another project; 'der Hain' (a grove) keeps the metaphor while signalling specificity. The lowercase German article 'der' next to capitalized 'Hain' makes the typography work — article reads as prefix, name stands as the proper noun.
session_note: Chad caught the favicon v1 looking like a shrub instead of three trees. Fix was structural (gaps + trunks) plus tonal (three different green tones), not just one or the other. Cloudflare deployment loop (push to main → live) makes visual iteration like this practical.
aha: Three trees needs structural gaps AND tonal variation — neither alone is enough
frustration_peak: v1 favicon looked like a shrub on the home screen — close but unmistakably wrong
wonder: Quadratic Bezier curves draw into a PNG using ray-casting and zero dependencies — the math is the library.

completed: iOS companion app skeleton scaffolded in ios/ subfolder — DerHain (WKWebView wrapper, full-screen, pull-to-refresh, external links route to Safari, dashboard stays in-app) + DerHainWidget (home screen widget, small + medium, fetches projects.json then top tracker priority via GitHub Contents API, refreshes 45min). SETUP.md walkthrough for Xcode project creation, target wiring, and wired-deploy to personal iPhone (no App Store, no TestFlight). CLAUDE.md updated with widget-schema-sync maintenance rule and iOS scope reflected in Out of Scope table.
learned: A WKWebView wrapper is the right intermediate step between PWA and full native rewrite — 95% of features stay web (auto-update on Cloudflare deploy, single codebase) while iOS-only platform integrations (widgets, Action Button, Keychain, native haptics) get added incrementally as native code only when they pay off. The widget extension is a separate target with its own bundle identifier and can't share code with the WebView app directly — it parses tracker JSON itself, so any schema change is a manual sync point. WKWebView's localStorage is isolated from Safari's, so PWA-installed users get a 'first launch' moment where the Gist sync rehydrates their notes. .xcodeproj files contain user-specific UUIDs and signing config — better to leave them out of git and have setup instructions reproduce them locally.
session_note: Chad isn't at his Mac, so all Swift was written 'cold' and committed; he'll open Xcode later and run through ios/SETUP.md. This is the first Swift code in the project-dashboard repo — first dual-platform project he's structured this way. The 'thin wrapper, web is source of truth' pattern is the explicit architectural commitment — keeps maintenance burden low while still unlocking iOS-only surfaces.
aha: WKWebView wrapper is the right intermediate step — keeps web as source of truth while unlocking iOS-only surfaces
wonder: Widget extensions are isolated processes with their own bundle ID — they really can't import from the main app's code, even if they're in the same Xcode project.
first_ever: First Swift code in this repo
curiosity_trail: Can the widget read locally cached tracker data instead of refetching every 45 minutes?

completed: Shipped der Hain iOS app + home-screen widget to physical iPhone. Built the Xcode project from the ios/ skeleton, signed with free Apple ID, walked through every Xcode 26 gotcha, deep-linked widget into the WKWebView, fixed icon, fixed widget background API. Also flattened der.hain. → derhain.chadstewartcpa.com to stay under Cloudflare Universal SSL.
learned: Xcode widget extension defaults to latest SDK deployment target regardless of parent app — caused the widget to silently filter out of the gallery on devices below the SDK. iOS 17+ widgets require .containerBackground(_:for:) modifier instead of setting a background view inside the body. Free Apple ID dev signing requires 'Embed Without Signing' (not 'Embed & Sign') for .appex extensions — and that dropdown only offers two options for extensions, never three. Cloudflare Universal SSL covers apex + one subdomain level only; nested subdomains need paid Advanced Certificate Manager.
session_note: Long, gauntlet-style session. Twelve+ Xcode dialogs, several false starts (folder collision when project name matched existing directory, target membership trap that put @main twice into the app module, deployment-target mismatch hiding the widget from gallery, missing AppIcon image showing default placeholder). Each fix was a single-line/single-checkbox change but finding the right one required reading the error message carefully and translating Apple's phrasing into actionable steps. End state: der Hain now lives on Chad's home screen with a working widget that pulls live data from GitHub every 45 minutes.
struggle: Xcode 26 introduced subtle defaults that broke the original SETUP.md instructions — widget Extension target deployment defaults to latest SDK, bundle ID derives case from Product Name, bridging-header dialog auto-pops on widget file add, and the New Target wizard has three new optional checkboxes (Live Activity, Control, App Intent) that scaffold collisions if left checked.
aha: The widget wasn't broken — iOS was filtering it out because its deployment target (auto-set to 26.4) exceeded what the phone could install. Once I matched it to the app's 17.6, the widget appeared in the gallery within seconds.
frustration_peak: When the widget finally showed up but threw 'Please adopt containerBackground API' on the home screen — felt like the goal post moved one more time after twelve previous fixes.
curiosity_trail: Could SETUP.md be retrofitted into a single Xcode-config check script (read project.pbxproj, flag deployment-target mismatch / target-membership doublings / missing icon images) so future fresh installs catch these before ⌘B?
first_ever: First iOS app shipped to a physical device + first widget extension built from scratch
wonder: A widget extension is just a .appex bundle nested inside the parent app's PlugIns/ folder — iOS scans those at install time and registers any whose Info.plist declares NSExtensionPointIdentifier = com.apple.widgetkit-extension. The whole 'add widget to home screen' flow is just iOS reading metadata from a sub-bundle.

completed: Closed the capture loop end-to-end: voice-dictate on iPhone via iOS Shortcut → POST to /api/inbox Cloudflare Pages Function → appended as Inbox-tagged note to the notepad Gist → next session-end Claude sweeps it into tracker priorities/shipped/backlog. Also made the tracker visual single-source — priorities/backlog/shipped lists hydrate from the #tracker-data JSON on page load, eliminating dual-edit. Plus codified session-end trigger phrases ('shipped X, next Y' / 'session-end' / 'sweep inbox') in CLAUDE.md.
learned: Inline <script> blocks execute as the HTML parser hits them — getElementById can't find sibling elements that appear later in the document. Hydration scripts that read embedded JSON must come AFTER the JSON <script> block. Caught this only by curling the deployed page and seeing the new banner render but the priority list still stale. Separately: iOS Shortcuts is a no-code automation runtime that ships in the OS; pairing it with a Cloudflare Pages Function gives voice-controlled API endpoints with zero auth UX (token stays server-side).
session_note: Started as a small ask — 'how do I update the tracker?' — and surfaced a real bug (visual HTML and JSON were dual-maintained, so the page showed stale priorities even after the JSON updated). Building the Inbox capture pipeline was the satisfying part: backend endpoint, walked Chad through Shortcuts setup, watched the first capture land in the gist via curl. The 'Now listening' artifact happened because Chad read the iOS dictation UI text out loud — the system literally captured itself describing itself.
struggle: Hydration bug was invisible from source — looked correct, but ran before the JSON <script> block was parsed so getElementById returned null and silently bailed. Only caught it by curling the deployed file and reading my own code back to myself.
aha: When 'Now listening Now listening' showed up in the gist, I thought it was a UI bleed — but Chad had read the iOS dictation prompt aloud. The capture system recorded itself describing itself. Felt like the universe winking back at the new pipeline.
frustration_peak: Pushing what I thought was a finished feature, watching Chad's screenshot still show the old priority list, and only finding the script-order bug by curling the live HTML.
curiosity_trail: What else wants to land in /api/inbox from the phone? Daily photo to a journal album? Location-tagged ideas? The endpoint is now a cheap landing pad for any iOS Shortcut.
first_ever: First voice-capture iOS Shortcut wired to my own backend — Action Button → Pages Function → Gist round-trip, all under a second
wonder: The full capture loop runs in maybe 800ms — phone dictates, HTTPS POSTs to Cloudflare's edge, Pages Function fetches the gist from GitHub, modifies it, PATCHes back, returns 200, phone shows notification. Four network hops across three services, voice-to-persisted-note in the time it takes to lower the phone.

completed: Widget v2 shipped to phone — Inbox count + shipped-today footer renders on medium size when either count > 0. Added WidgetCenter.reloadAllTimelines() to DerHainApp.onAppear so opening der Hain force-refreshes the widget instead of waiting on the 45-min OS timeline. Codified the interactive Inbox sweep as default protocol behavior with a 'sweep all' / 'session-end automated' opt-in for bulk mode, and saved as durable feedback memory across all future Claude sessions.
learned: WidgetCenter.shared.reloadAllTimelines() is the WidgetKit escape hatch from the OS-managed 45-min refresh cycle — call it from the parent app's .onAppear and you get a 'force-refresh' gesture for free (just open the app). Also: when proxying GitHub Gist PATCHes through a Cloudflare Pages Function, the WAF blocks default Python-urllib User-Agent — must set an explicit User-Agent string (curl -A or http.client headers) or requests get 403'd silently.
session_note: Continued from a 'how do I update the tracker?' question into a full home-screen feature: the widget now shows live Inbox + shipped-today counts, and reloads on app launch. Halfway through, Chad noticed I'd unilaterally swept his first Inbox captures earlier in the session and gave clear feedback: interactive review is the default; he wants to be the editorial hand. Saved as durable feedback memory + bulk-mode opt-in trigger added so the protocol respects autonomy without losing the option for hands-off sweeps. Whole loop is now visible on glass — voice → Inbox → widget badge → session-end review → tracker → push → widget reflects.
struggle: Xcode scheme picker dropped DerHain (the app scheme) from the visible list after we added the widget extension target — only DerHainWidgetExtension showed, blocking ⌘R from rebuilding the parent app. Took a Manage Schemes detour and Xcode quit/reopen to surface DerHain again.
aha: Seeing the widget on the home screen render '✓ 6 shipped today' for the first time — proof that the JSON I'd been editing in the terminal a minute earlier had propagated through Cloudflare to the OS widget timeline to the glass on Chad's lock screen. Sub-minute feedback loop from `git push` to phone display.
frustration_peak: Scheme picker showed only DerHainWidgetExtension — pressing ⌘R built/ran the widget extension scheme which has no installable app, so nothing happened on the phone. Had to walk Chad through Manage Schemes... to surface the DerHain scheme that should have been there by default.
curiosity_trail: What's the smallest unit of time between 'I had this thought' and 'it's reflected on glass?' Today: voice → ~800ms to gist → next session-end → push → 30s Cloudflare deploy → 45min widget timeline (or instant on app reopen). Could the gap shrink further with WidgetKit push (Live Activities) or a server-side webhook that nudges the widget directly?
first_ever: First time seeing my own work surfaced on a home-screen widget badge that updated in real time off a git push
wonder: The widget is just rendering JSON from a Cloudflare Pages deploy that came from a git push that came from an Edit tool call ten seconds before — but on the phone it feels alive, like the system is watching you. The illusion comes from collapsing four normally-asynchronous layers (commit, deploy, fetch, render) into a single sub-minute pulse.

completed: Inbox capture Shortcut now supports dual-mode — Choose from Menu prompts 'Speak' or 'Type' on launch; Speak runs Dictate Text, Type runs Ask for Input, both flow through a captureText variable into the same /api/inbox POST. Lets Chad capture silently in public spaces where talking to a phone is awkward.
learned: Choose from Menu's branch-result passthrough is finicky — the magic-variable handoff after End Menu can drop or default to a sibling action's output. Explicitly Set Variable to a named slot ('captureText') in each branch keeps the downstream POST step path-agnostic and reliable.
session_note: Tight follow-on session. Chad noted he doesn't always want to talk to his phone in public (the original Action Button shortcut was dictate-only) so we walked through editing the Shortcut in-place — added Choose from Menu above the existing actions, moved Dictate into the Speak branch, added Ask for Input under Type, and rewired the URL body. Tested both paths, both landed in the gist. Inbox swept at session-end.
struggle: Walking through Shortcut edits over text without seeing the screen — small UI words like 'Provided Input' vs 'Dictated Text' as magic variables matter a lot, and getting the drag-into-branch step right is hard to describe without a video.
aha: The right pattern wasn't 'detect cancellation' (fragile — Dictate Text doesn't cleanly distinguish silence from cancel) — it was 'ask the user upfront which mode they want.' Two taps to get explicit intent beats one tap with a guess.
curiosity_trail: What other modes might want a Choose from Menu wrapper? Photo capture (camera vs library)? URL capture (clipboard vs share sheet)? The pattern is: short menu of capture sources → Set Variable → unified POST.
wonder: The Action Button on iPhone is becoming a personal dispatcher — one physical button, n possible intents, branched at the Shortcut layer. The hardware is dumb; the routing is in software I wrote in ten minutes.

learned: Virtual categories cost nothing structurally — projName()'s `|| repo` fallback, dynamic chip rendering, and the dropdown JSON were already extension points. The only change was three lines in populateProjectSelects().
session_note: Small addition with outsized utility — Tasks now lets the Inbox-capture pipeline (Shortcut/widget) feed a real to-do list during sweeps. Future idea (parked in backlog): /api/inbox `?project=Tasks` param so the Shortcut can route directly without a sweep step.
